corrections.why: The facts and the story use the Register figure, 100 ft = 30.5 m (site visit 1/22/22). The 1954 survey's about 120 ft (36.6 m) is kept as a noted conflict, not a change. The editor should confirm the Register figure is the one to keep.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives 100 ft standing; the 1954 survey description gives about 120 ft. The story uses the Register figure, notes the survey figure, and does not settle which is current.

The Register and the survey place the tower in Independence County. The Encyclopedia of Arkansas places the community of Almond in northeastern Cleburne County and says Almond was in Independence County until 1883. The story keeps Independence for the tower and flags the community's county.

sources.title: Almond
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (centraluslookouts.weebly.com), reproducing a National Geodetic Survey station description

notes_for_editor: No build date in any source; the NHLR says Built Unknown and the 1954 survey description is the oldest source read. The first-flight removal is undated, so it is not in events. Brief elevation 361.5 m matches the Register's 1,186 ft (361 m) and the OSM tag of 361. The community's county (Cleburne) differs from the tower's (Independence) in the sources; the tower is about half a mile south of the settlement per the survey. No new photos.
